subject: Archaeology
title: Temples of Abu Simbel
description: A short lesson to help you apply Temples of Abu Simbel.

hook.text: Twice a year, sunlight reaches 200 feet into Abu Simbel and illuminates three of four statues in the sanctuary.

buildup.text: Ramesses II built the temple so sunlight hit the statues on February 22 and October 22 — likely key dates.

discovery.text: The fourth statue — Ptah, god of the underworld — is deliberately left in shadow. Darkness was part of the design.

twist.text: When the temple was moved in the 1960s, engineers could not perfectly replicate the alignment. It shifted by one day.

climax.text: Thousands of tourists gather twice a year to watch sunrise enter the temple. Ancient engineering still draws a crowd.

punchline.text: A pharaoh programmed sunlight 3,200 years ago. It still runs.

quiz.question: What happens twice a year at Abu Simbel?
options: The Nile floods the temple entrance in a ritual cleansing
Sunlight penetrates 200 feet and illuminates three sanctuary statues
Sand naturally clears from the entrance due to wind patterns

details.summary: Abu Simbel consists of two massive rock-cut temples built by Ramesses II in Nubia. The larger temple features four colossal seated statues of Ramesses. In the 1960s, the entire complex was cut apart and relocated to save it from the rising waters of Lake Nasser.
details.whyItMatters: Abu Simbel's relocation was one of the greatest engineering feats of the twentieth century. It demonstrated that international cooperation could preserve heritage, inspiring the UNESCO World Heritage program.
takeaways: Two rock-cut temples built by Ramesses II in Nubia
Four colossal statues of Ramesses guard the entrance
UNESCO relocated the temples in the 1960s to save them

faq.question: How were the Abu Simbel temples relocated?
faq.answer: Engineers cut the temples into over 1,000 blocks weighing up to 30 tons each, then reassembled them 65 meters higher on an artificial hill. The project took four years, cost $40 million, and involved engineers from over fifty countries.

faq.question: Why do the temples align with the sun twice a year?
faq.answer: On February 22 and October 22, sunlight penetrates the temple's inner sanctum to illuminate three of four statues. The god of the underworld, Ptah, remains in shadow. This solar alignment demonstrates the Egyptians' astronomical precision.
